methods.summary: Returns the pattern ID associated with this configuration if it is an anchored search for a specific pattern. Otherwise `None` is returned.

items.name: Input
items.summary: The parameters for a regex search including the haystack to search.

methods.name: anchored
methods.summary: Sets the anchor mode of a search.

methods.name: earliest
methods.summary: Whether to execute an "earliest" search or not.

methods.name: end
methods.summary: Return the end position of this search.

methods.name: get_anchored
methods.summary: Return the anchored mode for this search configuration.

methods.name: get_earliest
methods.summary: Return whether this search should execute in "earliest" mode.

methods.name: get_range
methods.summary: Return the span as a range for this search configuration.

methods.name: get_span
methods.summary: Return the span for this search configuration.

methods.name: haystack
methods.summary: Return a borrow of the underlying haystack as a slice of bytes.

methods.name: is_char_boundary
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if the given offset in this search's haystack falls on a valid UTF-8 encoded codepoint boundary.

methods.name: is_done
methods.summary: Return true if and only if this search can never return any other matches.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Create a new search configuration for the given haystack.

methods.summary: Returns true when the span in this match is empty.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the length of this match.

methods.summary: Create a new match from a pattern ID and a byte offset span.

methods.name: span

methods.name: start

items.name: MatchError
items.summary: An error indicating that a search stopped before reporting whether a match exists or not.

methods.name: gave_up
methods.summary: Create a new "gave up" error. The given `offset` corresponds to the location in the haystack at which the search gave up.

methods.name: haystack_too_long
methods.summary: Create a new "haystack too long" error. The given `len` corresponds to the length of the haystack that was problematic.

methods.name: kind
methods.summary: Returns a reference to the underlying error kind.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Create a new error value with the given kind.

methods.name: quit
methods.signature: fn quit(byte: u8, offset: usize) -> MatchError
methods.summary: Create a new "quit" error. The given `byte` corresponds to the value that tripped a search's quit condition, and `offset` corresponds to the location in the haystack at which the search quit.

methods.name: unsupported_anchored
methods.summary: Create a new "unsupported anchored" error. This occurs when the caller requests a search with an anchor mode that is not supported by the regex engine.

methods.name: capacity
methods.summary: Returns the total number of pattern identifiers that may be stored in this set.

methods.name: clear
methods.summary: Clear this set such that it contains no pattern IDs.

methods.name: contains
methods.summary: Return true if and only if the given pattern identifier is in this set.

methods.name: insert
methods.signature: fn insert(&mut self, pid: PatternID) -> bool
methods.summary: Insert the given pattern identifier into this set and return `true` if the given pattern ID was not previously in this set.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.summary: Return true if and only if this set has no pattern identifiers in it.

methods.name: is_full
methods.summary: Return true if and only if this set has the maximum number of pattern identifiers in the set. This occurs precisely when `PatternSet::len() == PatternSet::capacity()`.

methods.name: iter
methods.summary: Returns an iterator over all pattern identifiers in this set.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of pattern identifiers in this set.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Create a new set of pattern identifiers with the given capacity.

methods.name: try_insert
methods.signature: fn try_insert(&mut self, pid: PatternID) -> Result<bool, PatternSetInsertError>
methods.summary: Insert the given pattern identifier into this set and return `true` if the given pattern ID was not previously in this set.

items.name: PatternSetInsertError
items.summary: An error that occurs when a `PatternID` failed to insert into a `PatternSet`.

items.name: PatternSetIter
items.summary: An iterator over all pattern identifiers in a [`PatternSet`].

items.name: Span
items.summary: A representation of a span reported by a regex engine.

methods.name: contains
methods.summary: Returns true when the given offset is contained within this span.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.summary: Returns true when this span is empty. That is, when `start >= end`.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the length of this span.

methods.name: offset
methods.summary: Returns a new span with `offset` added to this span's `start` and `end` values.

methods.name: range
methods.summary: Returns this span as a range.
